errors.english: there is no inverted object in uncertain things such as (prameya) objects of cognition and so forth
errors.why: ma nges pa here is the inconclusive reason (anaikāntika) and gzhal bya nyid is the reason 'being knowable' (prameyatva), not 'uncertain things such as objects of cognition'.

fix.find: in uncertain things such as (prameya) objects of cognition and so forth
fix.replace: in inconclusive reasons such as (prameyatva) being knowable and so forth

errors.english: because it is not connected with the sound [note: the verbal designation or label]
errors.why: sgra is sound (śabda), the subject of the inference 'sound is permanent/impermanent because visible', not a verbal designation.

fix.replace: [note: sound (śabda), the subject of the inference]

errors.english: that which contradicts the reason becomes the proponent's proof and the opponent's refutation
errors.why: Two items are paired with two functions: the (valid) reason is the proponent's proof and the contradictory reason (viruddha) is the opponent's refutation.

fix.find: that which contradicts the reason becomes the proponent's proof and the opponent's refutation
fix.replace: the [valid] reason and the contradictory reason become, respectively, the proponent's proof and the opponent's refutation

note: The dialectic is roughly followed, but the logical terms (inconclusive reason, the subject 'sound', reason vs contradictory reason) are blurred, so the hetu-doctrine argument is hard to recover.

errors.english: the world they protected has been utterly destroyed and exhausted
errors.why: The world-protecting Protector is the Buddha; the blind beings bereft of him are ruined, they did not protect the world.

errors.english: What else could now be destroyed?
errors.why: The verse says that he whose foot-dust the gods placed on their heads is himself perishing, not a rhetorical question about what else could be destroyed.

note: A fluent rendering of the lament verses; two couplets have their referent misplaced.

errors.english: dappled animals, swans, and the like
errors.why: khra bo and ngang pa name varieties of individual cows (dappled, pale/goose-coloured), not 'dappled animals' and 'swans'.

note: The apoha argument on non-connection as a universal is rendered accurately and clearly.

errors.english: May those negative actions not ripen upon them!
errors.why: The point is that one owns one's own karma and their deeds do not ripen on oneself; it is a statement, not a wish for them.

errors.english: Even if executioners were to be dispatched, saying,
errors.why: The degenerate monks will even send executioners against those abiding in the Dharma, saying such dharmas no longer exist; it is a prediction, not a concessive clause.

note: The Śikṣāsamuccaya sūtra quotations and the Lotus verses are well rendered apart from two clauses in the first quotation.

errors.english: Being of the nature of mind, it is like an emanation, yet it is not an emanation of the gods.
errors.why: lta'i means 'should be regarded' (misread as lha 'gods'): the mind-made body is to be seen as like an emanation, but it is not an emanation.

fix.find: Being of the nature of mind, it is like an emanation, yet it is not an emanation of the gods.
fix.replace: Being mind-made (manomaya), it should be regarded as like an emanation, yet it is not an emanation.

errors.english: does their self-nature exist in this world
errors.why: bdag gi dngos po is ātmabhāva, the bodily existence (here the mind-made body), not 'self-nature'.

errors.english: The Blessed One also stated:
errors.why: bcom ldan 'das ma-r is a locative of the feminine Bhagavatī, a scripture cited as source, not 'the Blessed One stated'.

note: The argument on the bodhisattva's mind-made body is followed, but one misread syllable invents 'gods', and ātmabhāva and the cited source are mishandled.

errors.english: This is not stated as a contradiction in itself. Rather, it means that accepting a contradiction pertains to the object of certainty.
errors.why: gnod pa is invalidation (bādhā/bādhaka), not contradiction; the text says it is not called invalidating as such, but is accepted as invalidating with respect to an ascertained object, and the same mistranslation runs through the page.

fix.find: This is not stated as a contradiction in itself. Rather, it means that accepting a contradiction pertains to the object of certainty.
fix.replace: This is not stated to be invalidating (bādhaka) in itself; rather, it is accepted as invalidating with respect to an ascertained object.

errors.english: (Desire) original: 'dod pa refers to what is accepted
errors.why: The lemma 'dod pa here means 'asserted/held', which is why it is glossed by khas blangs pa; 'desire' is wrong.

errors.english: This is the view of the (Victorious One) original: rgyal ba can.
errors.why: rgyal ba can here names a commentator whose interpretation is reported, not the Buddha.

errors.english: For example, the treatise shows that there are no valid cognitions regarding the objects of comprehension.
errors.why: The statement 'pramāṇas having objects do not exist' is cited as the example common to treatise and one's own words; the treatise does not assert it.

note: The commentary on scriptural and self-invalidation is systematically mistranslated through 'contradiction' for gnod pa, and several lemmas are misread, so the argument is lost.

errors.english: These enter the person through the birth canal
errors.why: The offender enters the blazing iron animals through their genital passage and is burned in their bellies.

fix.find: These enter the person through the birth canal
fix.replace: The person enters these through their birth canals

errors.english: Great Lotus [note: original: Padmaniraya]
errors.why: The Great Lotus hell is Mahāpadma; Padma is the different hell named on the previous side.

note: A clear translation of the hell-punishment passage with one reversal of who enters whom.

errors.english: the digression that followed concurrently
errors.why: It is the digression that arose incidentally on the topic of auxiliary causes (sahakārin), not something 'concurrent'.

note: The argument against permanent causes receiving assistance from auxiliaries is accurately rendered.
The refutation of perception having universals as objects is correctly followed; a few dense lemma glosses are loosely worded but no clear error.

errors.english: following the conventions of that
errors.why: 'du byed is saṃskāra, the mental conditioning/impressions left by other treatises, not 'conventions'.

errors.english: due to the inferior nature of the treatises of the (tirthikas) non-Buddhist philosophers or others
errors.why: The inferiority is the people's (being duller than others), offered as an alternative to the influence of tīrthika treatises, not a property of the treatises.

note: The discussion of class and collective terms and co-reference is well handled, with two minor misreadings.
